articleTitle: Diffraction of a plane wave by a transparent wedge Zommerfeld - Malyuzhinetz approach
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: We consider a time-harmonic diffraction of a plane wave by a transparent wedge of an arbitrary opening by the Sommerfeld-Malyuzhinets approach, see e.g. [1]. The wave propagation velocities inside the wedge and outside are equal. An explicit solution is presented, which is studied asymptotically.

articleTitle: Kravchenko-Kotelnikov-Levitan-Wigner distributions in radio physical applications
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: In this article Kravchenko-Kotelnikov-Levitan-Wigner distributions are presented. These distributions are based on Wigner distribution in aggregate with generalized Whittaker-Kotelnikov-Shannon (WKS) series and Levitan polynomial constructed on basis of atomic functions (AF). The numerical experiments and physical analysis both have illustrated effectiveness of this approach for digital radar signal processing.

articleTitle: A fundamental mode of a nonplanar cavity with even or odd number of mirrors
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: We research optical multimirror ring-type cavities with a nonplanar contour. In such cavities, the propagation along the contour is accompanied with the rotation of coordinate axes on some angle. In case of odd number of mirrors an additional change of orientation also takes place. For cavities with an alone focusing element (a nonplanar mirror or a lens) we investigate stability conditions and the shape of a stability region in a space of dimensionless parameters. Cases of odd and even number of mirrors appear to be rather different. In case of stability, the cross-sectional distribution of the fundamental mode's field can be expressed in terms of the quadratic form's matrix with positively definite imaginary part. Having applied the method presented in, we obtain explicit analytical formulae for such matrices. There appears that the main directions of the focusing element coincide with such directions of the intensity ellipse or of the phase ellipse in cases of even or odd number of mirrors, respectively.

articleTitle: Extended Stationary Phase Method based on Fresnel functions for the calculation of three-dimensional scattering of electromagnetic waves from rectangular perfectly conducting plates
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present an extension over a novel three dimensional high frequency method for the calculation of the scattered electromagnetic (EM) field from a Perfect Electric Conductor (PEC) plate, which is based on the Physical Optics (PO) approximation and the Stationary Phase Method (SPM). This method has been presented only recently, showing fast and satisfactory results, nevertheless its accuracy around the area of the main scattering lobe may further be enhanced. The extension proposed here is utilizing higher order approximation terms, which imply the use of Fresnel functions in order to optimize the results without any load in time efficiency, since our initial goal is to present a complete analytical method that produces accurate results without sacrificing the calculation time, which is very important for the practical use of radio-propagation tools.

articleTitle: Diffractive model application for scattering radiation on turbulent atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Results of the analysis of intensity fluctuations characteristics of the radiation, scattered on optical non-uniformity of turbulent atmosphere (dynamic speckle - pattern) are presented in this work. Time coherence function and time frequency spectrum dependence on refraction index fluctuations are found by the suggested diffraction model of radiation scattering on phase medium non-uniformity. It is shown, that the refraction index fluctuation in the turbulence scales is determined only by wavelength and supervision geometry. Experimental data of root-mean-square value of the refraction index fluctuations of atmosphere turbulence measured along near-surface optical path is given below.

articleTitle: A boundary integral equation method in short-wavelength-to-period diffraction on multilayer 1D gratings and rough mirrors
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Diffraction problems by 1D multilayer structures having arbitrary border profiles including edges are considered at smallest wavelength-to-period ratios. The integral equation theory is so flexible that one can point out a few areas of its modifiability. In this work special attention is paid to physical models and low-level details, as well as to the generalization of the power balance criterion for the case of absorbing gratings. In the case of shallow gratings and mirrors, introducing speed-up terms produces an adverse numerical effect because of the ensuing uncontrolled growth of coefficients in analytically improved asymptotic estimations.

articleTitle: Diffraction from a layer of surface SH-waves radiated by a point source at the boundary
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The main part of elastic energy during underground and underwater blow-ups corresponds to the surface waves. This fact is connected to the fact that surface waves decay weaker than volume waves. Surface waves play big role in seismology and are observed constantly during every earthquake. In the present paper we will investigate the transformation of the elastic creeping wave of SH-polarization, for the wave going through the layer between two half-planes. In order to find the solution we use asymptotical method of boundary layer and the results of papers.

articleTitle: On the hyperbolic system with multiplicity more or equal to three
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Hyperbolic systems with noninvolutive multiple characteristics are considered and an example of ill-posed Cauchy problem is proposed.

articleTitle: Acoustic non-local permittivities in rigid-framed porous metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: What should be the most general macroscopic theory of sound propagation in a medium defined by a fluid in which rigid motionless solid inclusions are placed in periodic or stationary random manner? This, indeed, appears to be a very basic question of classical physics to which no complete answer has yet been provided. Based on considerations inspired by an apparently uncommon conception of the macroscopic electromagnetic theory, we suggest here what the general answer might be, in a special "slender fluid" case where the free-fluid bulk attenuation and the macroscopic fluid-solid shear reaction force are both neglected. In forthcoming work, our present conception of the macroscopic theories will be illustrated by the explicit construction of our two acoustical non-local "permittivities".

articleTitle: Generalization of the Biot's equations for account of fluid shear relaxation
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Based on the generalized variational principle the system of the generalized Biot equations is derived for consistent account of fluid shear relaxation. Account of shear viscosity relaxation leads to existence of a couple shear propagation modes additionally to a couple of longitudinal modes as in the Biot approach. At this the one shear mode is an acoustical one, while the other shear mode has diffusive behavior at low frequencies. Phase velocity and attenuation factor for the second shear mode linearly depend on frequency in the low frequency limit that is different from analogous behavior of diffusive longitudinal mode with the root frequency behavior of analogous values.

articleTitle: Time evolution of the wavelet transform of the acoustic field
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: In this paper we study the initial-value problem for a homogeneous acoustic wave equation in the two-dimensional space. Our approach is efficient if the initial data have multiscale structure and contain singularities and sharp edges. The wavelet transform is known to be a proper transform for analyzing such functions. We present a formula which describes the evolution with time of the wavelet transform of the spatial distribution of a solution. Our approach does not require an explicit calculation of the solution itself. A numerical example of the multiscale approach to the wave propagation is presented.

articleTitle: Random groups and the theory of optical fiber light guides
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: We present a review of main results obtained with a new approach to analytical and numerical investigation of influence of random inhomogeneities on light propagation in a single-mode fiber light guide (SMFLG). An approach is based on the theory of random groups and allows to obtain in frame of accurate mathematical model some mathematically rigorous and physically meaningful results on the statistical characteristics of complex amplitudes of electric field of light wave. The approach allows also to provide the numerical simulation of these statistical characteristics when rigorous results can not be obtained. The proofs of mathematical assertions presented may find in [1].

articleTitle: Quantum gate implementation based on nonlinear optical phenomena
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The quantum optical gate CCNOT based on five level atomic scheme is discussed. The qubits are encoded by single photon packets polarization. The nonlinear cross Kerr effect is used for getting nonlinear phase shifts in these beams.

articleTitle: On plane wave scattering off a system of scatterers
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The scattering of a plain wave on a system of scatterers is considered. The scatterer is described as a bounded domain Omega with the velocity of the wave propagation in the interior of Omega be different from the velocity of wave propagation in the exterior of Omega. The T-matrix formalism has been developed for description of a scattering process. The multichannel approach of Faddeev equations is applied to the problem of calculation of the T-matrix in order to obtain the multiscattering series for the scattering amplitude. The onefold and twofold rescattering amplitudes which in certain cases give the leading contribution to the overall scattering amplitude have been calculated analytically as for nonregular placement of the scatterers as well as for the periodic two dimensional grid of scatterers.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of multipactor discharge in microwave waveguides
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: We present a brief review of methods of simulation of secondary emission discharge (multipactor) in electromagnetic devices of different geometry. Our approach takes into account effects of random secondary emission velocities on the steady-state of multipactor. Methods discussed are based as on exact analytical solutions for the arrival time probability density of secondary electrons, as on the direct Monte Carlo calculation for more complex systems, such as electrodynamic waveguides.

articleTitle: The interaction of the surface waves in the composite layer
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The linear stage of parametric instability of electromagnetic surface waves guided by the planar composite layer with metal walls is investigated. This instability can arise due to the presence of an external time-harmonic magnetic field oriented parallel to the slab boundary if the space-time condition between the interaction waves takes place. The instability growth rate is determined.

articleTitle: Wavelet-based field theory and cross-scale correlations
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: We consider application of continuous wavelet transform to the field theory of the fields phi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">alpha</sub>(x) depending on both the position x and the resolution a. The correlation functions langphi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">alpha</sub>(x)phi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">alpha'</sub> (x')rang for such fields may be finite at x = x'. In case of the gauge fields the nonlocality of the wavelet transform makes the theory more complicated, but the gauge symmetry for each scale is observed. This approach provides a possibility to estimate the causal effect of the large-scale wave envelope to the small scale entities. The same approach can be applied to the Langevin-type stochastic differential equations, treated within the framework of quantum field theory, time series analysis etc.

articleTitle: Transient waves produced by Gaussians transverse sources in a dispersive medium
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Solutions for the inhomogeneous telegraph equation corresponding to the Gaussian transverse sources are constructed. Relations describing the transient waves are obtained.

articleTitle: Gaussian symmetry of the paraxial wave equation
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Starting from the expression of the optical paraxial wave equation we investigate a particular Gaussian symmetry applying a Lie Group formalism.

articleTitle: Helmholtz solitons: Maxwells equations, interfaces, bistability & counterpropagation
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: We give a brief overview of some new results in Helmholtz soliton theory. Firstly, fundamental considerations are made in terms of new contexts for Helmholtz solitons that arise directly from Maxwells equations. We then detail applications of Helmholtz solitons in material interface geometries: generalising Snells law to nonlinear beams and reporting new qualitative phenomena. Novel families of bistable soliton solutions to a cubic-quintic Helmholtz equation are also presented. Finally, an analysis of counterpropagating beams that includes new bidirectional solitons is summarized. This paper is dedicated to the late Dr. Valery E. Grikurov.

articleTitle: Effective thermal conductivity of ceramic blocks with inner ducts
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The joint work with Valery Grikurov on thermal conductivity is recollected. This article has been written by one author only (S.Yu.S) but he dared to do it taking into account two reasons Firstly, it gives him the opportunity to recollect his scientific and human communications with late Valery Grikurov. Secondly, it permits him to discuss on an informal level how local characteristics of a media can be generalized to global characteristics of an element. This discussion also can be extended to diffraction problems.

articleTitle: Inversion of the logarithmic integral operator defined on several arcs of a circle and its application to diffraction theory
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The inversion of the logarithmic integral operator defined on several curves is considered. Formulas for the inverse operator and its action on trigonometric functions are obtained. The results are applied to a problem of diffraction by a conducting cylinder with longitudinal slots.

articleTitle: Acoustic scattering by a thin cylindrical screen with the Dirichlet boundary condition and the impedance boundary condition on opposite sides of the screen
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: A problem on scattering acoustic waves by a thin cylindrical screen is studied. In doing so, the Dirichlet condition is specified on one side of the screen, while the impedance boundary condition is specified on the other side of the screen. The solution of the problem is subject to the radiating condition at infinity and to the propagative Helmholtz equation. By using the potential theory the scattering problem is reduced to a system of singular integral equations with additional conditions. By regularization and subsequent transformations, this system is reduced to a vector Fredholm equation of the second kind and index zero. It is proved that the obtained vector Fredholm equation is uniquely solvable. Therefore the integral representation for a solution of the original scattering problem is obtained.

articleTitle: Excitation and propagation of whistler waves in a magnetoplasma in the presence of a cylindrical duct with decreased density
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Excitation and propagation of whistler-mode waves in an unbounded magnetoplasma in the presence of a cylindrical duct with decreased plasma density are studied. Using a rigorous solution for the total source-excited field comprising both the discrete and continuous parts of the spatial spectrum of waves, the radiation resistance of a source in the form of a loop antenna is determined. Conditions have been revealed under which the power radiated from the loop antenna immersed in a decreased-density duct is dominated by the contribution of either discrete-or continuous-spectrum modes.

articleTitle: The Dirichlet problem for the propagative Helmholtz equation in a 2-D exterior domain bounded by closed curves and open arcs
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The Dirichlet problem for the 2-D Helmholtz equation in an exterior domain bounded by closed curves and open arcs is studied. The existence of classical solution is proved by potential theory. The problem is reduced to the Fredholm equation of the second kind and index zero, which is uniquely solvable. It means, that the solution can be computed by standard codes.

articleTitle: About the formation of regular damages inside widebandgap dielectrics under pulses of femtosecond laser radiation
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The recently published experimental results about influence of femtosecond laser on widebandgap dielectrics are discussed in this paper. We propose the possible mechanism of formation regular microvoids along filament path inside glass, based on interference of surface plasmon-polaritons on boundary metallized dielectric-glass in condition of nonthermal phase transition in dielectric.

articleTitle: Prograde Rayleigh-wave particle motion for simple models
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The existence of prograde particle motion for fundamental-mode Rayleigh waves is studied systematically in models of increasing complexity by using an exact expression of the ellipticity. The models studied are: the well-known half-space, the impedance surface with Tiersten's boundary conditions (TBC), layer with fixed bottom (LFB) and layer over half-space (LOH). It turns out that only the models layer with fixed bottom and layer over half-space may support prograde Rayleigh-wave motion on the surface under certain conditions which are analyzed carefully. The exact expression for the ellipticity of Rayleigh waves, together with the secular equation for the phase velocity, are useful to find the most relevant parameters for prograde particle motion, namely Poisson's ratio in the layer and the shear-wave velocity contrast between the layer and the half-space. The density contrast between layer and half-space, and up to a certain degree Poisson's ratio in the half-space, are usually less important. The domain of existence of prograde Rayleigh-particle motion is specified for typical combinations of parameters. These considerations are not only of general theoretical interest but they are also important in applying the so-called H/V-method (H/V = ratio between horizontal and vertical displacement components of Rayleigh waves) for seismic hazard assessment.

articleTitle: Longitudinal wave scattering on tunnel cylindrical cavity with hard inclusions of radial cross-section in isotropic media
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: It is presented numerical-analytical technique for solving boundary-value problems concerned the diffractional elastic waves scattering on tunnel cylindrical cavities. The cavities are partially tight by inclusions of radial cross-section. The technique is based on the wave field expressions for general body. The calculations were carried out when the inclusion occupies both left-hand and right-hand cavity's side. During the investigation the relative wavelength and the physical specifications as well as the size of inclusion were changed.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of a profile function using the knowledge of the nonsymmetric intensity of X-rays diffraction in thin films
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The method of reconstruction of a profile function in thin films by X-ray diffraction experiments is extended to asymmetric diffraction pattern.

articleTitle: On the statement of the three-dimensional Neumann-Kelvin problem
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The classical three-dimensional Neumann-Kelvin problem of the linear theory of ship waves is considered and its statement is investigated with particular attention to the conditions at infinity. The general eigensolution to the problem in empty half-space (in absence of bodies) is derived. This solution allows us to formulate correct conditions at infinity both for the Green function and for the potential of the problem, describing motion of submerged bodies.

articleTitle: Wave modes in periodic systems of thin tubes
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The problem of wave propagation in a periodic system of thin tubes is studied. The waves are described by the dispersion diagrams, i.e. by the dependencies of the propagation constants on the temporal frequency. The main question under consideration is how many modes can propagate in a particular system. The paper presents a method of finding the dispersion diagrams, and an inequality for the number of modes, linking the number of modes with the topological properties of the system.

articleTitle: Some aspects of the calculating schemes correctness in users positioning in radionavigating systems
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: We consider a problem of a radio wave propagation from space apparatus to user's equipment, from the point of view of navigating tasks. In our investigation of correctness of the calculating schemes, methods of equivalent in extended meaning transformations were used. Main variable characteristics were determined by geometrical factor of the system ldquospace apparatus almanac-users equipmentrdquo.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic waves generated by line exponentially decaying current pulses propagating in lossy media
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The structure of transient electromagnetic radiation generated by line exponentially decaying current pulses propagating in lossy media is investigated. Description of the emanated waves in the space-time domain is obtained transferring the initial electromagnetic problem to a scalar one, separating the radial variable, using the Riemann formula and reducing the final multiple-integral solution into a simple quadrature taking advantage of the specific form of the integrand.

articleTitle: Asymptotic expansion of SV type surface waves for singular propagation directions in transversely isotropic elastic media
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The general scheme of constructing the uniform asymptotics of SV type surface modes as the sum of space-time (ST) caustic expansion and two correction ST ray series (with complex eikonals) is applied to an inhomogeneous transversely isotropic elastic medium. The case is considered where at certain points on the boundary surface S (or at a curve which lies on S) the phase velocities of two quasi-shear elastic waves turn out to be identical. Here, on S, the elasticity tensor depends on four material parameters rather then five parameters as is commonly the case with transversely isotropic media.

articleTitle: Solution of light scattering problem for multilayered nonspherical particles
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: We suggest an efficient extension of the separation of variables method (SVM) to the case of scatterers with multiple layers. Two possible computational schemes are described and their numerical analysis and comparison with the extended boundary conditions method (EBCM) are done. The new approach is shown to provide highly accurate results for simple shape particles (e.g., spheroids, Chebyshev particles) with a large number of layers (10 and more). Such scatterers cannot be efficiently treated by any of other exact methods.

articleTitle: Waves running along a periodic set of small inhomogeneities in fluid loaded thin elastic plate
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Waves localized along a periodic set of point-wise inhomogeneities in a thin elastic plate, are studied. Both the case of point masses and holes of small radius in isolated and in fluid-loaded elastic plates are considered. Point models of attached masses and generalized point models of holes are used.

articleTitle: Method of neural networks committees in calculation of time series maximal Lyapunov exponents
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The present paper deals with modification of the neural networks estimation method of the maximal Lyapunov exponent (MLE) for chaotic time series and development of this method for processing series with real world application. Namely, the necessity to use committees of neural networks for MLE calculation is strongly grounded. The method of estimating the Lyapunov exponent calculation error is elaborated. The technique of forecasted trajectories divergences averaging on the delayed pseudoattractor of time series is introduced. The separation of two important cases when MLE is zero and the case when it is small but positive is accomplished by making use of appropriate statistical tests. It is shown that even the modified method of neural networks committee MLE estimation can give positivity of MLE for stochastic series at relatively high statistical characteristics of the neural networks forecasts quality. Additional tests and researches for identification chaos in time series are required. The proposed approach is tested on the model chaotic and periodic time series as well on time series having real world application such as EEG signals and tensotremorogram signals.

articleTitle: The L(c, n) numbers and their application in the theory of waveguides
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The theorem for existence and for the basic properties of the L(c, n) numbers (positive real numbers, coherent with the positive purely imaginary zeros zeta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k,</sub> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(c)</sup> in x of the complex Kummer confluent hypergeometric function Phi(a, c; x) with a = c/2 - jk - complex, c - real, (c ne l, l = 0, -1, -2, -3,...), k - real, x = jz, z - real, positive and n = 1, 2, 3,...), is formulated and proved numerically. It is composed of three lemmas. Lemmas 1 and 2 demonstrate the existence of quantities and determine them in case c ne l and c = l (in which Phi(a, c; x) is not defined) as the common limits of the couples of infinite sequences of positive real numbers {K_(c, n, k)_)} and {M_(c, n, k_)}, (K_(c, n, k_) = |k_|zeta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k_,</sub> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(c)</sup>, M_(c, n, k_) = |a_|zeta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k_,</sub> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(c)</sup> for k_ rarr -infin, and {L(l - epsiv, n)} and {L(l + epsiv, n + 1)}, (epsiv - infinitesimal positive real number) for epsiv rarr 0, resp. (The subscript ldquo-rdquo indicates quantities, corresponding to negative k.) Lemma 3 reveals the main features of the numbers (recurrence relation, formula for symmetry and bond of some of them with the Ludolphian number). Tables and graphs illustrate the influence of parameters c and n on L(c, n). The benefit of numbers is manifested in the theory of azimuthally magnetized circular ferrite waveguides, propagating normal TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</sub> modes.

articleTitle: [Front cover]
publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: wavelet-based field theory; transient waves; Helmholtz solitons; thermal conductivity; multilayer 1D gratings; whistler waves; magnetoplasma; acoustic nonlocal permittivities; plane wave diffraction; optical fibre light guides; quantum gate implementation; and surface waves.

publicationTitle: 2008 Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction
abstract: Recounts the life and  professional achievements of Valery E. Grikurov.
